posts.title: Spiced Pumpkin Soup
posts.meta_description: Pumpkin, caramelized onion, ginger, cumin and green chili are simmered in vegetable stock, puréed smooth and finished with nutmeg and herbs.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.115
posts.body_markdown:
Spiced Pumpkin Soup builds its flavor in two stages: first the onion is softened, then garlic, ginger, cumin, and optional green chili are cooked with it until the onion becomes caramelized.

Pumpkin is then simmered in vegetable stock until tender enough to purée. The source includes optional maple syrup, which can round the pumpkin without making the soup noticeably sweet.

Nutmeg and chopped cilantro or parsley are used at the end rather than cooked into the soup. That keeps the garnish aromatic and lets the pumpkin remain the central flavor.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons good oil
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end, optional
- 4 cups vegetable stock
- 4 cups pumpkin, cubed
- 1 teaspoon maple syrup, optional
- 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, for garnish
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro leaves or parsley, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the onion and sauté for about 4 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, and optional green chili and continue until the onion is caramelized, about 4 minutes more. Add the vegetable stock and pumpkin and cook until the pumpkin is soft, about 10–15 minutes. Stir in the optional maple syrup, purée carefully until smooth, then garnish with nutmeg and cilantro or parsley. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Sona’s Zucchini Soup
posts.meta_description: Zucchini and caramelized onion are simmered with vegetable bouillon, puréed smooth and served with a spoonful of yogurt in this simple soup.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.116
posts.body_markdown:
Sona’s Zucchini Soup is deliberately simple, relying on caramelized onion and zucchini rather than a long list of spices. That makes the texture and sweetness of the vegetables easy to notice.

The zucchini cooks briefly under a lid before the water and bouillon are added. Once the vegetables are soft, the soup is puréed rather than left chunky.

Salt, pepper, and optional cayenne are adjusted at the end. A spoonful of plain yogurt finishes the bowl and adds a cool, creamy contrast to the warm soup.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1 cup onions, sliced
- 2 cups zucchini, sliced
- 3 cups water
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, optional
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
- 4 tablespoons plain yogurt, for garnish

## Method
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the onions and sauté until caramelized, about 7–8 minutes. Add the zucchini, cover, and cook for 3–4 minutes. Add the water, bouillon, and optional cayenne, raise the heat to a boil, then reduce to low and simmer until the zucchini is soft, about 5–6 minutes. Purée carefully until smooth, season with salt and pepper, and garnish with yogurt. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Spinach Vegetable Soup
posts.meta_description: Spinach, sweet potato and carrot simmer with onion, ginger and cumin in a straightforward vegetable soup designed for a hearty everyday bowl.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.116
posts.body_markdown:
Spinach Vegetable Soup keeps the vegetables distinct instead of blending them. Onion and ginger are sautéed first, then cumin is warmed briefly before the liquid is added.

Sweet potato and carrot provide the body of the soup, while a generous amount of chopped spinach adds freshness and color. The vegetables cook together until the sweet potato is tender.

The seasoning is restrained: bouillon, salt, pepper, ginger, and cumin. The source suggests serving the soup with bread, which suits its simple, substantial character.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 cup onions, sliced
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 2 cups water
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 1 cup sweet potatoes, cubed
- 1/2 cup carrots, sliced
- 5–6 cups spinach, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions and ginger and sauté until the onions begin to caramelize, about 5 minutes. Stir in the cumin and cook for 1 minute. Add the water, bouillon, sweet potatoes, carrots, and spinach and cook until the sweet potatoes are softened, about 15 minutes. Season with salt and pepper and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Beat the Cold Soup
posts.meta_description: A deeply seasoned vegetable soup with ginger, garlic, chili, garam masala, mushrooms, zucchini, broccoli and cauliflower in vegetable stock.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.117
posts.body_markdown:
Beat the Cold Soup is a layered vegetable soup whose title reflects the author’s personal context, not a medical guarantee. Its culinary strength comes from building flavor step by step in the pot.

Onion, ginger, chili, garlic, celery, carrot, and dry spices are sautéed in stages before mushrooms, zucchini, tomato, stock, peppercorns, and cloves are added. Broccoli and cauliflower go in later so they do not overcook.

Lemon juice is added just before the soup is finished, giving the broth a brighter final note. Whole peppercorns are removed before serving and cilantro is used as the garnish.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1/2 cup onions, chopped
- 3 teaspoons fresh ginger, minced
- 2 teaspoons fresh green chilies, minced
- 2 teaspoons garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup celery, diced
- 1/2 cup carrots, diced
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/2 cup mushrooms, chopped
- 3/4 cup zucchini, chopped
- 1/4 cup tomatoes, diced
- 2 cups vegetable stock
- 4 whole peppercorns
- 2 cloves
- 1 cup mixed broccoli and cauliflower florets
- Juice of 1 lemon
- Salt to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions, ginger, and chilies and sauté about 4 minutes. Add the garlic and celery and cook a few minutes, then add the carrots, cayenne, turmeric, and garam masala and continue briefly. Add mushrooms and zucchini for 1 minute, then tomatoes for another minute. Add stock, peppercorns, and cloves and simmer 10 minutes. Add broccoli and cauliflower and cook about 7 minutes more. Stir in lemon juice and salt, remove the peppercorns, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Yummy Yam Soup
posts.meta_description: Yams simmer with caramelized onion, garlic, turmeric and whole warm spices, then are puréed into a smooth soup finished with yogurt and parsley.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.118
posts.body_markdown:
Yummy Yam Soup gets its depth from a combination of ghee, olive oil, caramelized onion, garlic, and whole warm spices. The yams provide most of the body.

Cinnamon, clove, peppercorns, and turmeric simmer with the yams until everything is soft. The source specifically suggests checking the consistency and adding more water if the soup becomes too thick.

The cinnamon stick is removed before blending. Yogurt and parsley are added only at serving, giving the smooth soup a cool and fresh finish.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon ghee or butter
- 1 teaspoon olive oil
- 3/4 cup onions, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, sliced
- 6 cups yams, cubed
- 1 tablespoon vegetable bouillon powder
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 cinnamon stick, about 2 inches long
- 1 clove
- 2 whole peppercorns
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 6 cups water
- 4 tablespoons plain yogurt, for garnish
- 4 teaspoons fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Heat the ghee and olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the onions and sauté about 4 minutes, then add the garlic and continue until the onions are caramelized, about 4 minutes more. Add the remaining ingredients except the garnishes, bring to a boil, reduce to low, and simmer about 20 minutes. Adjust the seasoning and consistency, adding water if needed. Remove the cinnamon stick, purée carefully until smooth, and garnish with yogurt and parsley. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Spinach & Sweet Potato Soup
posts.meta_description: Spinach and sweet potato are simmered with onion, ginger and garlic, then puréed only partly so the finished soup keeps some texture.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.119
posts.body_markdown:
Spinach & Sweet Potato Soup uses very little liquid relative to the vegetables, which gives it a thick, substantial texture without relying on cream.

Onion, ginger, and garlic are sautéed first, then sweet potato and spinach cook together under a lid until the potato is tender. The soup is puréed, but the source leaves it slightly chunky.

Pepper and garam masala are stirred in after blending. That keeps the final spice note clear and lets the sweet potato and spinach remain recognizable.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 cup onions, chopped
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 3 1/2 cups sweet potatoes, cubed
- 5–6 cups fresh spinach, chopped
- 1 1/2 cups water
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- Freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon garam masala, or to taste

## Method
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions, ginger, and garlic and sauté until the onions begin to caramelize, about 5 minutes. Add the sweet potatoes, spinach, water, and salt, cover, and cook until the sweet potatoes are softened, about 15–20 minutes. Purée carefully until fairly smooth but still a little chunky. Stir in pepper and garam masala and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Immune-Boosting Shiitake Mushroom & Vegetable Soup
posts.meta_description: Dried shiitake mushrooms, sweet potato, carrot, cabbage and optional miso form a hearty vegetable soup with ginger, garlic and tamari.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.120
posts.body_markdown:
This shiitake mushroom and vegetable soup is titled “Immune-Boosting” in the source; here the emphasis stays on the recipe rather than making a medical claim. Dried shiitakes create both the broth and much of the savory character.

The soaked mushrooms are sautéed before onion, carrot, sweet potato, cabbage, garlic, and ginger are layered into the pot. Their reserved soaking liquid then becomes the soup base.

Spinach, tamari or Bragg seasoning, and optional miso are added near the end. Green onion is used as a fresh garnish, while the vegetables remain chunky rather than blended.

## Ingredients
- 12 dried shiitake mushrooms
- 6 cups water, for soaking
- 1–2 tablespoons good oil
- 1 tablespoon sesame oil
- 3/4 cup onions, chopped
- 1 cup carrots, chopped
- 2 cups sweet potatoes, cubed
- 1 cup Chinese cabbage or other cabbage, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 teaspoons fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 cup spinach leaves, chopped, optional
- 1/3 cup Bragg seasoning, tamari, or soy sauce
- 1/4 cup miso paste, optional
- Freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup green onions, sliced, for garnish

## Method
Soak the shiitake mushrooms in 6 cups water for 30 minutes. Remove and thinly slice them, reserving the soaking liquid. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat, sauté the mushrooms for a few minutes, then add the sesame oil and onions and cook 2–3 minutes. Add carrots and sweet potatoes for 2–3 minutes, then cabbage, garlic, and ginger, cover, and cook 2 minutes. Add the reserved mushroom broth and simmer until the vegetables are soft, about 20–25 minutes. Stir in the optional spinach, Bragg or tamari, optional miso, and pepper, cook until the spinach wilts, garnish with green onions, and serve. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Asparagus Miso Soup
posts.meta_description: Asparagus and sweet potato simmer in vegetable bouillon before miso, lemon and pepper are added, then the soup is lightly mashed and garnished.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.121
posts.body_markdown:
Asparagus Miso Soup combines sweet potato and asparagus in a broth that is lightly mashed rather than fully puréed. That preserves some texture in the final bowl.

Onion and ginger are sautéed first, then dissolved bouillon and sweet potato simmer before the asparagus is added. The asparagus cooks only until the vegetables are just tender.

Miso is stirred in toward the end until fully dissolved, followed by lemon, pepper, optional cayenne, and final seasoning. Yogurt or sour cream is used as a garnish.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon olive oil
- 1/4 cup onions, chopped
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 2 tablespoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 3 cups hot water
- 2 cups sweet potatoes, diced
- 2 cups asparagus, chopped
- Freshly ground pepper to taste
- Pinch of cayenne pepper, optional
- Squeeze of lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon miso paste
- Salt or soy sauce to taste
- 1 tablespoon plain yogurt or sour cream, for garnish

## Method
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions and ginger and sauté about 4 minutes. Dissolve the bouillon in the hot water and add it to the pot with the sweet potatoes. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook 10 minutes. Add the asparagus and cook 5–10 minutes more. Stir in pepper, optional cayenne, lemon juice, and miso until the miso dissolves. Adjust the seasoning with salt or soy sauce, adding water if the soup is too salty. Remove from the heat, lightly mash while leaving some texture, garnish with yogurt or sour cream, and serve. Makes 4 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Warming Cauliflower, Broccoli & Miso Soup
posts.meta_description: Cauliflower and broccoli simmer with caramelized onion, garlic, chili and whole spices, then are partly puréed and finished with miso.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.122
posts.body_markdown:
Warming Cauliflower, Broccoli & Miso Soup starts with caramelized onion, garlic, and optional green chili before the vegetables are added.

Cauliflower and broccoli simmer with cloves and cinnamon until tender. The whole spices are removed before the vegetables are puréed, and the source intentionally leaves the texture slightly chunky.

Miso is stirred in after blending rather than boiled aggressively. Extra hot water can be added if a thinner consistency is preferred.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 1 cup hot water
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 cups onions, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced, or to taste
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 5 cups cauliflower florets
- 4 cups broccoli florets
- 3 1/2 cups water
- 3 cloves
- 1 cinnamon stick, about 2 inches long
- 1/4 cup miso paste
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Dissolve the bouillon in 1 cup hot water and set aside. Heat the olive oil in a medium pot over medium-low heat, add the onions, and sauté about 4 minutes. Add the chilies and garlic and continue until the onions are caramelized, about 4 minutes more. Add the cauliflower, broccoli, and 3 1/2 cups water, raise the heat to a boil, then add the cloves and cinnamon. Reduce to low and simmer 15–20 minutes. Remove the cloves and cinnamon, purée until fairly smooth but still slightly chunky, then stir in the miso until dissolved. Add hot water if needed, season with salt and pepper, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Miso Soup with Tofu, Green Onions & Seaweed
posts.seo_title: Miso Soup with Tofu, Green Onions & Seaweed | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A quick miso soup with tofu, green onion and black seaweed, finished with a dash of cayenne and prepared in only a few minutes.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.123
posts.body_markdown:
This miso soup is extremely quick because the water and seaweed are brought to a boil before the heat is turned off. The miso is then dissolved without prolonged boiling.

Medium tofu and chopped green onion add substance, while a small amount of black seaweed gives the broth a distinct mineral and savory character.

A dash of cayenne finishes the bowl. The source recommends hijiki or arame and notes that the dried seaweed can also be presoaked before cooking.

## Ingredients
- 4 1/2 cups water
- 1 tablespoon thin black seaweed
- 4 tablespoons miso paste
- 1/4 cup medium tofu, cubed
- 2 green onions, white parts only, chopped
- Dash of cayenne pepper

## Method
Combine the water and seaweed in a large pot over high heat and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, add the miso, and stir until completely dissolved. Stir in the tofu, green onions, and cayenne and serve immediately. Makes 4 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Hearty Red Lentil, Barley & Vegetable Soup
posts.seo_title: Red Lentil, Barley & Vegetable Soup | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Red lentils, barley, vegetables and warm spices simmer together in a hearty one-pot soup with tomato, parsley, bay leaf, cloves and peppercorns.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.124
posts.body_markdown:
Hearty Red Lentil, Barley & Vegetable Soup builds its base by sautéing onion, garlic, ginger, celery, and dry spices before the water goes in.

Barley needs a longer cooking time than red lentils, so it is added first with the herbs and whole spices. The lentils go in later and cook until soft.

The result is a substantial one-pot meal with both grain and legumes. Bay leaves and peppercorns are removed before serving so the broth keeps their flavor without leaving whole spices in the bowl.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons olive oil
- 1/2 cup onions, chopped
- 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 cup celery, diced
- 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 cup carrots, sliced
- 3/4 cup tomatoes with liquid, chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 4 whole peppercorns
- 3 cloves
- 4 cups water
- 1/4 cup barley
- 1/2 cup red lentils

## Method
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions, garlic, ginger, and celery and sauté for 1 minute. Add coriander, cumin, cayenne, and turmeric and cook 2 minutes, then add the carrots and cook 2–3 minutes. Add the tomatoes and juice and cook a few minutes more. Add parsley, bay leaves, salt, peppercorns, cloves, water, and barley and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes. Stir in the red lentils, reduce to a simmer, and cook about 25 minutes until soft. Remove the bay leaves and peppercorns before serving. Makes 4–6 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Red Lentil Soup
posts.meta_description: Red lentils cook with onion, ginger, garlic, celery, carrot and whole warm spices in a fast, comforting soup finished with fresh cilantro.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.125
posts.body_markdown:
Red Lentil Soup is designed for speed. The vegetables are chopped finely, allowing the lentils and aromatics to soften together in under half an hour.

Onion, garlic, ginger, celery, and carrot are sautéed before the red lentils, water, bouillon, cloves, peppercorns, and cinnamon are added.

Whole spices are removed once the lentils are soft. Salt and pepper are adjusted at the end, and chopped cilantro adds a fresh finish.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1/2 cup onions, finely chopped
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 cup celery, finely chopped
- 1/2 cup carrots, finely chopped
- 2/3 cup red lentils
- 6 cups water
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 2 cloves
- 3 whole peppercorns
- 1 cinnamon stick, about 2 inches long
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1 tablespoon fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions, garlic, and ginger and sauté for 1 minute. Add the celery and carrots and cook 3–4 minutes. Add the lentils, water, bouillon, cloves, peppercorns, and cinnamon and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 20–25 minutes until the lentils are soft. Remove the cinnamon stick and peppercorns, season with salt and pepper, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Sprouted Mung Bean Soup
posts.meta_description: Sprouted mung beans simmer in vegetable stock with onion, ginger, chili and celery, then are finished with fresh lime for a simple legume soup.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.126
posts.body_markdown:
Sprouted Mung Bean Soup keeps the ingredient list short and lets the sprouted beans carry most of the dish. Onion, ginger, chili, and celery form the aromatic base.

Vegetable stock and sprouted mung beans are brought to a boil, then immediately reduced to a gentle simmer. The source gives a 20–30 minute cooking window.

Lime juice is stirred in at the end rather than simmered. The source also offers optional yogurt, tamarind chutney, cilantro, or cilantro-garlic chutney variations for serving.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1/4 cup onions, chopped
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced
- 1/4 cup celery, chopped
- 4 cups vegetable stock
- 3 cups sprouted mung beans
- Juice of 1/2 lime

## Method
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onions, ginger, and green chilies and sauté for 1 minute. Add the celery and continue cooking 5–6 minutes, until the onions are caramelized. Add the vegetable stock and sprouted mung beans, bring to a boil, then immediately reduce to low and simmer 20–30 minutes until done. Stir in the lime juice and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Spicy Chickpea Soup with Coconut, Cilantro & Yogurt
posts.seo_title: Spicy Chickpea Soup with Coconut & Yogurt | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Chickpeas, coconut milk and warm spices simmer with curry leaves, then part of the soup is puréed and finished with tamarind and cilantro yogurt.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.127
posts.body_markdown:
Spicy Chickpea Soup with Coconut, Cilantro & Yogurt is a partly blended soup, so it keeps both creamy body and whole chickpeas in the bowl.

The seasoning is developed in stages: caramelized onion, popped mustard seeds, garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander or cumin, then chickpeas and curry leaves in stock.

Half of the soup is puréed with coconut milk and returned to the pot. Tamarind chutney adds a sweet-sour finish, while cilantro mixed with yogurt is spooned over each serving.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/2 tablespoons good oil, for the onions
- 3/4 cup onions, chopped
- 1 1/2 tablespoons good oil, for the mustard seeds
- 1 teaspoon black mustard seeds
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon turmeric
- 2 teaspoons ground coriander or cumin
- 2 cups chickpeas, cooked or canned
- 3 cups vegetable stock
- 6 curry leaves
- 1/2 cup coconut milk
- 2 tablespoons tamarind chutney, or 2 tablespoons lemon juice plus 1 teaspoon maple syrup
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish
- 1/2 cup plain yogurt, for garnish

## Method
Heat 1 1/2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium-low heat and sauté the onions until caramelized, about 6–8 minutes. Push them aside, add the remaining oil and mustard seeds, cover, and let the seeds pop for 30 seconds. Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric, and coriander or cumin and cook 3–4 minutes. Add the chickpeas, then stock and curry leaves, and simmer 15–20 minutes. Transfer half the mixture, without the curry leaves, to a blender with the coconut milk and purée until smooth, then return it to the pot. Stir in the tamarind chutney and discard the curry leaves. Mix the cilantro and yogurt separately and use as a garnish. Makes 4–6 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Deb’s Hearty Chickpea Soup
posts.meta_description: Chickpeas, cabbage, potatoes and tomatoes make a substantial soup, with part of the chickpeas blended into stock for a naturally thicker texture.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.128
posts.body_markdown:
Deb’s Hearty Chickpea Soup combines whole chickpeas with a second portion that is puréed into vegetable stock, creating thickness without relying on cream.

Onions and garlic are softened first, then tomatoes, grated cabbage, potatoes, and stock simmer until the vegetables are tender. Whole chickpeas are added directly to the soup.

A purée of additional chickpeas and stock is stirred in afterward. Lemon juice, sweet paprika, parsley, and optional salt finish the pot and sharpen the hearty vegetable base.

## Ingredients
- 2 tablespoons good oil
- 3 cups onions, chopped
- 4 teaspoons garlic, minced
- 1 cup water
- 4 cups tomatoes, diced
- 8 cups cabbage, grated
- 3 potatoes, diced
- 4 cups vegetable stock
- 2 cups chickpeas, cooked or canned
- 4 cups vegetable stock, for the purée
- 2 cups chickpeas, cooked or canned, for the purée
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons sweet paprika
- 2 cups fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt to taste, optional

## Method
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions and garlic and sauté a few minutes, then add 1 cup water and continue until the onions soften. Add the tomatoes, cabbage, potatoes, and 4 cups stock, reduce the heat, and simmer 15–20 minutes until the vegetables are soft. Stir in 2 cups chickpeas. Separately, purée the remaining 4 cups stock with the remaining 2 cups chickpeas until smooth and pour into the soup. Add more stock if the soup is too thick, then stir in lemon juice, paprika, parsley, and optional salt. Makes 8–12 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Chilled Cucumber & Coconut Soup
posts.meta_description: Cucumber, coconut, mint, cilantro, lime, ginger and yogurt create a chilled soup with fresh herbs, cooling texture and a lightly spiced finish.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.129
posts.body_markdown:
Chilled Cucumber & Coconut Soup begins by seasoning the cucumber before blending. Garlic, ginger, mint, cilantro, chili, lime, and cumin are mixed in and chilled for several hours.

After that rest, the cucumber mixture is puréed with grated coconut. Yogurt is stirred in afterward rather than blended from the beginning, preserving a creamy but fresh texture.

If the soup is too thick, the source suggests adding a small amount of water. Cilantro and cayenne are used only as the final garnish.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups cucumbers, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 2 cloves garlic
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves, chopped
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 cup coconut, grated
- 2 cups plain yogurt
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, for garnish

## Method
Combine the cucumbers, salt, garlic, ginger, mint, cilantro, chilies, lime juice, and cumin in a bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 3–4 hours. Purée the chilled mixture with the grated coconut in a blender or food processor. Pour into a serving dish and stir in the yogurt until smooth. If too thick, add about 1/4 cup water. Garnish with cilantro, sprinkle with cayenne, and serve chilled. Makes 4 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Kathy’s Gazpacho
posts.meta_description: Kathy’s Gazpacho blends tomato, cucumber, celery, red pepper, avocado, parsley and lime into a chilled summer soup finished with yogurt.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.130
posts.body_markdown:
Kathy’s Gazpacho is built entirely from fresh vegetables and herbs, with no cooking stage. Garlic and jalapeño are minced first, then the other vegetables are pulsed in gradually.

Tomato juice or V8 supplies extra liquid, while lime juice and flaxseed or hemp oil provide acidity and body. Avocado makes the texture richer without turning the soup heavy.

The soup is chilled before serving and finished with yogurt and parsley. The source keeps the texture quite smooth but still relies on pulsing rather than prolonged blending.

## Ingredients
- 2 cloves garlic
- 1 large jalapeño pepper
- 2 cups cucumbers, roughly chopped
- 2 celery stalks with leaves, sliced
- 1 red bell pepper, roughly chopped
- 1 small red onion, sliced
- 4 tomatoes, sliced
- 1 avocado, roughly chopped
- 1 cup fresh parsley, roughly chopped
- 1 cup tomato juice or V8 juice
- 1/2 cup fresh lime juice
- 1/4 cup flaxseed oil or hemp oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin, or more to taste
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
- A few parsley sprigs, for garnish
- 1 cup plain yogurt, for garnish

## Method
Mince the garlic and jalapeño in a blender or food processor. Add the cucumbers, celery, red bell pepper, onion, and tomatoes and pulse. Add the avocado, parsley, tomato juice, lime juice, oil, cumin, salt, and pepper and pulse until quite smooth. Refrigerate until thoroughly chilled, then garnish each serving with yogurt and parsley. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Chilled Mixed Fruit Soup
posts.meta_description: Strawberries, nectarines, plums and berries are simmered with peach nectar, sweetener and cinnamon, then chilled with fresh fruit folded back in.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.131
posts.body_markdown:
Chilled Mixed Fruit Soup uses two textures of fruit. A small portion is reserved fresh, while the rest is simmered with peach nectar, water, sweetener, and cinnamon.

The cooked fruit is puréed until smooth, then the reserved strawberries, nectarine, blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries are added back while the soup is still hot.

After cooling, the soup is refrigerated until chilled. Yogurt and fresh mint are used as garnishes, giving the sweet fruit base a creamy and herbal finish.

## Ingredients
- 3 cups strawberries, quartered
- 3 nectarines, pitted and diced
- 3 plums, pitted and chopped
- 2 1/2 cups blueberries
- 1 cup raspberries
- 1 cup blackberries
- 1 1/2 cups peach nectar
- 3 cups water
- 6 tablespoons agave nectar or other sweetener
- 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon
- 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt, for garnish
- Fresh mint sprigs, for garnish

## Method
Reserve 1/2 cup strawberries, 1 nectarine, 1 cup blueberries, and all of the raspberries and blackberries in a large bowl. Place all remaining fruit, peach nectar, water, sweetener, and cinnamon in a large pot and bring to a boil. Reduce to low and simmer about 15 minutes until the fruit is soft, then purée carefully until smooth. Return to the pot and add the reserved fruit while the soup is still hot. Cool, cover, and refrigerate until chilled, about 30 minutes. Garnish with yogurt and mint. Makes 10 servings.

posts.title: Kala Channa in Coconut Sauce
posts.seo_title: Kala Channa in Coconut Sauce | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Black chickpeas simmer in a spiced tomato and coconut sauce with curry leaves, lemon and caramelized onion in this rich Indian-style entrée.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.140
posts.body_markdown:
Kala Channa in Coconut Sauce uses black chickpeas, which have a firmer texture and earthier flavor than common pale chickpeas. The source cooks them separately before building the sauce.

Mustard seeds are popped in oil, followed by tomato, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander, cayenne, turmeric, and salt. Coconut milk and curry leaves then turn the spiced tomato base into a richer sauce.

Caramelized onions are prepared separately in ghee and olive oil and folded in near the end. Lemon juice provides the final acidity before the curry leaves are removed.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup dried black chickpeas
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1 teaspoon mustard seeds
- 2 cups tomatoes, diced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- Salt to taste
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 4–5 curry leaves
- Juice of 1 lemon, or tamarind chutney
- 1 cup onions, thinly sliced
- 1 teaspoon ghee or butter
- 1 teaspoon olive oil

## Method
Soak and cook the black chickpeas according to the source’s bean-cooking method. Heat the good oil in a large pot over medium-high heat, add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander, cayenne, turmeric, and salt, reduce to medium, and cook 8–10 minutes until the tomatoes soften. Add the cooked chickpeas, coconut milk, and curry leaves and cook 10–15 minutes more. Stir in lemon juice and remove from the heat. Separately, caramelize the onions in ghee and olive oil over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, then add them to the chickpeas. Remove the curry leaves and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Chickpea Curry
posts.meta_description: Chickpeas finish cooking in a spiced onion and ginger sauce with turmeric, cumin, coriander and garam masala, then are brightened with lemon.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.141
posts.body_markdown:
Chickpea Curry starts with chickpeas that are already partly cooked, so the final simmer can finish them directly in the seasoned liquid.

Onion, ginger, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and cayenne are sautéed before the chickpeas and reserved cooking water are added. This lets the spices coat the beans rather than sitting only in the broth.

Lemon juice is stirred in once the chickpeas are tender but not mushy. Cilantro is used as the garnish and salt is adjusted at the end.

## Ingredients
- 1 2/3 cups dried chickpeas
- 1 1/2 cups reserved chickpea cooking water
- 2 tablespoons good oil
- 1/4 cup onions, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/2 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Soak and cook the chickpeas until about two-thirds done, reserving 1 1/2 cups of the cooking water. Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat and sauté the onions 3–4 minutes until they begin to brown. Add the ginger, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and cayenne and cook 1 minute. Add the chickpeas and reserved water, bring to a boil, reduce to medium, and simmer about 20 minutes until the chickpeas are tender but not mushy. Stir in the lemon juice, adjust the salt, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Aunty Zee’s Masala Patties (or Dokri Nu Shak)
posts.meta_description: Gram-flour patties are cooked, cooled and cut into squares, then warmed in a spiced tomato masala and finished with a yogurt mixture.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book pp.142–143
posts.body_markdown:
Aunty Zee’s Masala Patties, also called Dokri Nu Shak, is a two-part dish: cooked gram-flour patties and a tomato-based masala sauce.

The patty mixture is whisked into boiling water and cooked until thick, then spread into a square, cooled completely, and cut. The source emphasizes sifting the flour and whisking to prevent lumps.

The masala is built from mustard seeds, cumin, chilies, curry leaves, tomato, ginger, garlic, spices, lemon, and tomato paste. Yogurt, water, and a little gram flour are added only just before serving.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups gram flour
- 3/4 cup onions, chopped
- 2–3 fresh green chilies, chopped
- 1 1/2 teaspoons dhanna jeera
- 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
- Juice of 1 lemon or lime
- 1/4 cup grapeseed oil or good oil
- 1 teaspoon black mustard seeds
- 1/2 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 2 dried red chilies
- 6–8 curry leaves, optional
- 2 cups tomatoes, diced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 3/4 teaspoon ground cumin
- 3/4 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
- Juice of 1 lemon or lime
- 1 tablespoon tomato paste
- 2 cups plain yogurt
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tablespoon gram flour
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
For the patties, sift the gram flour into a medium bowl, add the onions, green chilies, dhanna jeera, salt, and lemon or lime juice, and mix well. Bring 4 cups water to a boil, add the patty mixture, reduce to low, and whisk continuously for 10–15 minutes until bubbling and thick. Spread into a lightly greased 12-inch square, cool completely, and cut into 1 1/2-inch squares. For the masala, heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, dried chilies, and optional curry leaves, cover for 30 seconds, then add the remaining masala ingredients except yogurt, water, gram flour, and cilantro. Reduce to medium-low and cook 15–20 minutes until oil appears on the surface. Add the patties and coat gently. Before serving, whisk the yogurt, water, and gram flour until smooth, add to the pan, and heat on low about 5 minutes. Garnish with cilantro. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Tea Party Channa Bateta
posts.meta_description: Potatoes and chickpeas are sautéed with mustard seeds, turmeric, chili, cilantro and lemon for a compact Indian tea-party dish.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.144
posts.body_markdown:
Tea Party Channa Bateta combines boiled potato and chickpeas with a direct mustard-seed tempering. The result is substantial enough for a main course but compact enough for tea-time serving.

Mustard seeds are popped first, then potatoes are sautéed with turmeric, green chili, cayenne, cilantro, and salt. Chickpeas are added only after the potatoes have taken on the spices.

Lemon juice and a small amount of sweetener finish the dish. The source suggests mashing a small portion and stirring it back in if a thicker consistency is wanted.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon good oil
- 1/2 teaspoon black mustard seeds
- 1 1/2 cups potatoes, boiled and cubed
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1 1/2 cups chickpeas, cooked or canned
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon sweetener

## Method
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Immediately add the potatoes, turmeric, green chilies, cayenne, cilantro, and salt and sauté 2–3 minutes. Add the chickpeas and cook 2 minutes more. Stir in the lemon juice and sweetener. For a thicker texture, mash about 1/4 cup of the potato-and-chickpea mixture separately and stir it back into the pot. Makes 2 servings.

posts.title: Quick Black Beans
posts.meta_description: Black beans are combined with zucchini, peppers, spinach, ginger, garlic and chili, then served with yogurt and cilantro for a quick meal.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.145
posts.body_markdown:
Quick Black Beans turns cooked beans into a fast vegetable-rich meal. Onion, ginger, garlic, and chili form the first layer of flavor, followed by zucchini, peppers, and spinach.

Tamari or salt and chili sauce provide the seasoning. The vegetables cook under a lid only briefly, so they soften without losing all of their structure.

The black beans are added at the end just to heat through. Yogurt and cilantro are used as the final garnish, giving the bowl a cool and fresh contrast.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1 teaspoon sesame oil
- 3/4 cup onions, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh green chilies, chopped
- 1 cup zucchini, quartered and sliced
- 1 cup yellow bell peppers, diced
- 1 cup red bell peppers, diced
- 2 cups spinach
- Tamari or salt to taste
- Chili sauce to taste
- 2 cups black beans, cooked
- 1/2 cup plain yogurt, for garnish
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Heat the good oil and sesame oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions, ginger, garlic, and green chilies and sauté 1–2 minutes. Add the zucchini, yellow pepper, red pepper, spinach, tamari or salt, and chili sauce. Cover, reduce to medium, and cook 4–5 minutes. Add the cooked black beans and stir until heated through. Serve in bowls with yogurt and cilantro. Makes 2 servings.

posts.title: Small Red Bean Curry
posts.meta_description: Small red beans finish cooking with caramelized onion, ginger, garlic, tomato, coriander, cumin and garam masala, then are brightened with lemon.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.146
posts.body_markdown:
Small Red Bean Curry starts with beans that are cooked only about two-thirds of the way, allowing them to finish in the seasoned tomato mixture.

Onion, ginger, and garlic are caramelized first, followed by coriander, cumin, and garam masala. Fresh tomato is cooked until soft before the entire mixture is added to the beans.

Lemon juice is stirred in only after the beans are fully tender. Cilantro finishes the dish, while the source also notes that kidney beans or azuki beans can be substituted.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups dried small red beans
- 2 tablespoons good oil
- 1 cup onions, minced
- 2 tablespoons fresh ginger, minced
- 2 teaspoons garlic, minced
- 2 teaspoons ground coriander
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon garam masala
- 1 1/2 cups fresh tomatoes, cubed
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 3 tablespoons fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Soak and cook the red beans until about two-thirds done. Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat, add the onions, ginger, and garlic, reduce to medium, and sauté until the onions are caramelized, about 5–6 minutes. Add coriander, cumin, and garam masala and cook 30 seconds. Stir in the tomatoes and cook about 5 minutes until soft. Add this mixture to the beans and continue cooking 15–20 minutes until the beans are tender. Stir in lemon juice, adjust the salt, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 6 servings.

posts.title: Doug’s Favorite Beans
posts.meta_description: Black-eyed peas simmer with peppers, coconut milk, lemon and warm spices, then are finished with a slow-cooked onion, chili and ginger vagar.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.147
posts.body_markdown:
Doug’s Favorite Beans combines black-eyed peas with coconut milk, bell peppers, lemon, and a separate onion-based vagar. The beans and seasoning are cooked in two parallel stages.

The peas simmer with green chili, ginger, turmeric, salt, and optional kombu until almost tender. Red and green peppers, coconut milk, lemon juice, and optional gur are added only near the end.

The vagar is cooked separately and slowly so the onions become deeply caramelized. It is poured over the beans just before serving, with chopped cilantro added as the final garnish.

## Ingredients
- 3 cups dried black-eyed peas
- 9 cups water
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end
- 3 slices fresh ginger
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 2 teaspoons salt
- 1 stick kombu, optional
- 2 large red bell peppers, cubed
- 2 large green bell peppers, cubed
- 2 cups coconut milk
- 6 tablespoons lemon juice, or to taste
- 1 tablespoon gur or brown sugar, optional
- 1 tablespoon ghee
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 cups onions, sliced
- 1 tablespoon fresh green chilies, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
For the beans, combine the black-eyed peas, water, whole green chili, ginger slices, turmeric, salt, and optional kombu in a large pot and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer and cook until the beans are almost done, about 40 minutes. Add the bell peppers, coconut milk, lemon juice, and optional gur and cook about 10 minutes more. For the vagar, heat the ghee and olive oil in a frying pan over medium-low heat, add the onions, minced chilies, and ginger, and cook slowly until caramelized, up to 30 minutes. Pour the vagar over the finished beans, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 8–10 servings.
